children: New Zealand-based retailer Briscoe's 1H Ebit beat Macquarie's forecasts, but the bank stays at neutral as it waits for evidence of a sustained recovery in earnings and profit margins. Briscoe has now achieved three consecutive quarters of sales growth. Still, Macquarie points out that its "earnings recovery remains constrained by weak discretionary spending, elevated promotions, and margin pressure." Briscoe's gross margin fell by 58 basis points to 40.9%. Macquarie says the slower deterioration in margin suggests profitability is cyclically impaired, rather than due to structural issues. Its price target falls 3% to NZ$4.70/share. Briscoe is unchanged at NZ$4.35 today. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
